items.q: The renal plasma flow used as the denominator of the filtration fraction on this page is given as:
opts: 700 ml
125 ml
605 ml
items.exp: FF = GFR ÷ renal plasma flow, with the note RPF = 700 ml, estimated using para amino hippuric acid (PAH). (Book p738)

items.q: Fill up: The numerator of the printed fraction 125/700 is the ______.
opts: GFR
RPF
Filtration coefficient
SnGFR
items.exp: The worked line is = 125 / 700 = 0.1 to 0.2, i.e. GFR over renal plasma flow. (Book p738)

items.q: Following the arrows for a raised filtration fraction, the correct sequence on this page is:
opts: ↑ peritubular capillary oncotic pressure → fluid taken from the interstitial space → ↓ renal interstitial HP → ↑ reabsorption from PCT
↑ renal interstitial HP → ↑ peritubular oncotic pressure → ↓ reabsorption from PCT
↓ peritubular capillary oncotic pressure → ↑ renal interstitial HP → ↓ reabsorption
↑ reabsorption from PCT → ↓ filtration fraction → ↑ renal interstitial HP
items.exp: ↑ FF → ↑ peritubular capillary OP (d/t more filtration) → taken in fluid from interstitial space → ↓ RIHP → ↑ reabsorption from PCT. (Book p738)

items.q: A cirrhotic patient with low effective arterial volume has a raised filtration fraction. Applying this page's chain, proximal tubular reabsorption is expected to:
opts: Increase, because peritubular capillary oncotic pressure is high while interstitial pressure is low
Decrease, because interstitial hydrostatic pressure is low
Increase, because the PCT oncotic pressure falls
Remain unchanged, as filtration fraction does not touch reabsorption
items.exp: The chain drawn under filtration fraction links a raised FF to higher peritubular capillary oncotic pressure, removal of fluid from the interstitium, a fall in RIHP and therefore increased PCT reabsorption. (Book p738)

items.q: The printed theory of pressure natriuresis concludes that a raised cardiac output cannot produce a sustained rise in blood pressure unless there is renal impairment.
opts: True — the sentence is written immediately after the ↑CO line
False — a raised cardiac output sustains pressure whatever the kidney does
True — and the page writes the identity as BP = CO ÷ PVR
False — the theory concerns water diuresis only, not sodium
items.exp: As printed: ↑ CO leads to ↑ excretion of Na+ & H2O; therefore ↑ CO cannot produce sustained ↑ in BP unless there is renal impairment (BP = CO × PVR). (Book p738)
